records.statement: The fictional facility is new, privately operated, one story, and sprinklered.
records.limitations: This is a fictional profile fact and does not establish a construction, fire-protection, permit, or occupancy determination.

records.statement: The fictional facility is in the Town of Horseheads, Chemung County, New York, outside every incorporated village and outside New York City.
records.limitations: No real address or parcel is represented; actual territorial and agency jurisdiction would require verification.

records.statement: For this laboratory exercise, the Town code-enforcement authority is the assumed local authority having jurisdiction.
records.limitations: Actual agency jurisdiction, adopted editions, amendments, enforcement authority, agreements, and permit responsibility remain subject to controlled-source verification.

records.statement: The flagship space is a research laboratory and is not healthcare, pharmaceutical compounding, semiconductor production, pilot manufacturing, or full production.
records.limitations: The assumed use does not determine legal occupancy, hazardous-material, process, or permit classification.

records.statement: The intended fictional occupancy assumption is Group B research-laboratory use.
records.limitations: This is not a verified legal classification; use, hazards, quantities, control areas, fire areas, and building configuration require qualified review.

records.statement: The process uses bench-scale alumina-based ceramic powder and sintered ceramic specimens for weighing, wet mixing, preparation, and characterization.
records.limitations: No product formulation, safety data sheet, CAS identity, additive content, particle-size distribution, or exposure assessment has been selected.

records.statement: The maximum open powder batch is 250 g.
records.limitations: This is a simulation inventory bound and does not establish compliance with a hazardous-material, exposure, fire, or permit threshold.

records.statement: The maximum powder inventory in the laboratory is 5 kg in closed containers.
records.limitations: This is a simulation inventory bound and does not establish compliance with a hazardous-material, exposure, fire, or permit threshold.

records.statement: The scoped material is noncombustible and nonreactive but presents a particulate inhalation and contamination concern.
records.limitations: This project assumption does not replace a supplier safety data sheet, hazard classification, exposure assessment, or industrial-hygiene review.

records.statement: The proof excludes combustible dust, flammable-gas processes, flammable-liquid processes, explosives, pyrophoric materials, water-reactive materials, oxidizers, highly toxic gases, radioactive materials, biological agents, classified electrical locations, and quantities intended to produce a high-hazard occupancy.
records.limitations: The exclusions bound the fictional proof; they do not establish that a real product or process lacks these hazards.

records.statement: The scoped zones are the corridor, transition or airlock, and process laboratory already represented by the flagship topology.
records.limitations: This restates the accepted fictional topology and does not establish a physical design or code-required separation.

records.statement: The intended pressure direction is corridor to transition or airlock to process laboratory.
records.limitations: No numerical differential-pressure criterion, tolerance, persistence interval, or recovery interval is approved.

records.statement: A dedicated process-exhaust system serves the process enclosure and laboratory.
records.limitations: The arrangement is synthetic project intent and is not represented as a legally applicable requirement or approved physical design.

records.statement: Exhaust passes through monitored particulate treatment before outdoor discharge.
records.limitations: Treatment is an owner or project dependency; no specific code requirement, technology, efficiency, or test criterion is established.

records.statement: Two VFD-driven fans form a duty and standby pair, and either fan can provide the intended normal duty.
records.limitations: This is qualitative synthetic design intent; no capacity, response-time, transfer, or availability criterion is approved.

records.statement: The shared exhaust path and treatment unit are common dependencies that a standby fan cannot replace.
records.limitations: This describes the fictional dependency model and does not establish a physical failure analysis or code-required redundancy architecture.

records.statement: A supply or makeup-air subsystem supports the intended pressure cascade.
records.limitations: No airflow balance, control sequence, capacity, pressure, or response criterion is approved.

records.statement: FacilityOps remains read-only toward external systems and must never issue a command or configure a controller.
records.limitations: Observed or synthetic command and request indications remain evidence only and do not establish execution or physical response.
